matches.rationale: GT1 concerns incorrect ordering and improper definition of orthogonal matrices P_k and Q in Equation (1) breaking the ISVD encryption logic. No finding addresses matrix ordering, orthogonality properties, or the invertibility issues in Eq 1; pred_id 1 concerns Eq 5 leverage scores, pred_id 10 concerns Algorithm 1 logic gaps, neither matching the ISVD mechanism flaw.

GT2 identifies that Equation (5) leverage score computation (e_{i,j}^T U_k) is ill-formed and ambiguous. Pred_id 1 directly addresses Eq 5, explaining that the leverage scores as printed are degenerate (all equal to 1) due to using full orthogonal U, making the importance mechanism invalid—this captures the same underlying scientific issue of broken leverage score logic in Eq 5.

GT3 concerns lack of clarity on replay buffer budget M enforcement across clients and missing baseline replay sample details in Tables 2/3, undermining experimental transparency. Pred_id 5 and 6 address table structure/column mismatches and missing TinyImageNet beta=0.1 data, but do not discuss memory budget allocation or baseline replay sample specification—different issues.

GT4 criticizes omission of variance/standard deviation for TinyImageNet results in Tables 2 and 3, harming data integrity. Pred_id 5 identifies that the TinyImageNet beta=0.1 column is entirely empty in Table 3 for all methods including FedCBDR, and notes structural inconsistencies—this directly captures missing/incomplete TinyImageNet reporting in the same tables.

GT5 argues Section 5.2 exaggerates claims of 'adaptability and robustness' given uneven/marginal gains and lack of failure-case analysis. None of the findings critique the interpretation or rhetoric of the results discussion in Section 5.2; pred_id 12 concerns a sentence fragment in 5.5, not claim distortion.

GT6 concerns fabrication of future-dated or unverifiable references ([5], [6], [8], [12], [13]) in Related Work. No finding discusses reference validity, citation dates, or fabrication of background literature.

GT7 identifies omission of ethical approval, consent, or privacy safeguards discussion in the Experiments section. None of the findings mention ethical integrity, IRB approval, or data consent issues.

GT8 critiques overpromising rhetoric in the Abstract ('achieves balanced class-wise sampling ... improves generalization' without qualifiers). No finding addresses the Abstract's rhetorical style or overstated language; pred_id 11 concerns terminology inconsistency, not rhetorical manipulation.

GT9 identifies that the Conclusion overstates effectiveness ('significantly improves') inconsistently with limitations and marginal gains shown in Experiments/Ablation. No finding discusses the Conclusion section or cross-section narrative misalignment between Conclusion and experimental results.

GT10 concerns selective omission and inconsistent reporting of variance/baseline results in Tables 2, 3, and 5, harming data integrity. Pred_id 5 documents missing TinyImageNet beta=0.1 data for all methods in Table 3 and structural inconsistencies across Tables 2/3—directly capturing selective/incomplete reporting in the same tables.

GT11 identifies inconsistent application of temperature scaling in Equations (7) and (9), with unclear concatenation and conflicting loss definitions. Pred_id 7 directly addresses the incompatibility between Eq 7 and Eq 9, explaining differences in normalization and softmax support—matching the same underlying inconsistency in the TTS loss formulation.

GT12 argues Section 5.3 ablation overstates TTS module's standalone effect given marginal gains within variance. No finding critiques the interpretation or claims in Section 5.3 ablation discussion; pred_id 12 concerns a sentence fragment in 5.5, not ablation claim distortion.

GT13 concerns omission of baseline hyperparameter tuning details, computational budgets, and run-time comparisons in Section 5.1, impairing reproducibility. No finding discusses missing tuning methodology, resource trade-offs, or computational cost transparency in the experimental protocol.

GT14 identifies selective reporting in Section 5.6 hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, excluding poor-performing settings and biasing robustness interpretation. No finding addresses Section 5.6, Figure 4, or selective omission of extreme hyperparameter results.

GT15 identifies Abstract's claim of 'global coordination mechanism' as overstated relative to the Method's privacy-constrained pseudo-feature aggregation, creating narrative inconsistency. No finding discusses the Abstract's global-perspective claim or its misalignment with the actual method's limited global view.
